Fall River Reservoir Dam — Model Setup Progress

State Dam ID 070129 · Clear Creek County, Colorado · Hazard Class: High · Report generated 2026-07-29

This is a MODEL SETUP PROGRESS report, not a computed inundation map. No HEC-RAS hydraulic simulation has been run yet — the map below shows real terrain, the real reservoir footprint, and the real extracted dam-crest alignment, but does not show a computed flood extent. See the Status section below for exactly what has and hasn’t been done, and docs/preliminary_disclaimer.md for the full PE-review requirement that applies to every output from this toolkit.

Real 2021 LiDAR terrain (hillshade), the reservoir’s real footprint at normal pool elevation (10,835 ft), and a candidate dam-crest alignment extracted from the same terrain and visually confirmed. No flood extent is shown because none has been computed.

Status — what’s actually done

  • Real 2021 LiDAR terrain ingested and built into a DEM
  • Elevation-area-storage curve derived from terrain, anchored to reported storage near crest (documented approximation, flagged per-row)
  • Breach parameters computed (Froehlich 2008, MacDonald & Langridge-Monopolis, Washington State — piping failure mode)
  • Dam-crest alignment extracted from terrain and visually confirmed
  • Normal pool elevation sourced from the dam’s own 2025 EIR (freeboard figure)
  • HEC-RAS project created; terrain attached; 2D flow area, reservoir storage area, and breach connection all built in the real geometry file
  • Plan file and Unsteady Flow Data (boundary conditions) — not yet created
  • 2D mesh generation
  • HEC-RAS hydraulic computation (the actual breach simulation)
  • Post-processing (depth grid, inundation extent polygon)
  • Downstream structures / population-at-risk overlay
  • Final EAP-ready inundation map

Breach parameter estimate — Froehlich (2008), piping failure mode

ParameterValue
Average breach width91.2 ft

Formation time0.246 hr (≈14.8 min)

Two other empirical methods (MacDonald & Langridge-Monopolis, Washington State) were also computed and both collapse to a sub-2-ft breach width with plausibility warnings tripped — consistent with the dam’s 2025 GEI Consultants risk assessment identifying internal erosion/piping, not a full breach, as the dominant threat. A PE must select the appropriate method before this feeds any real hydraulic run.
